proof_summary: At \(n=56\) and \(n=60\), direct arithmetic gives the same triple \((92,4,2)\), whereas \(2^2\) divides both numbers, so the original construction treats them as the distinct values \(56\) and \(60\). Consequently the triple transform reuses at \(60\) the first-appearance label from \(56\), namely \(41\), while the original transform assigns the new label \(42\).
